title: Internal file paths leaked in an error message
root_cause: The error sent to the client embeds the exact internal path and the raw strerror() text. Neither corrupts memory, but both hand an attacker a map of the server's internals -- the leak is in what gets disclosed, not in a bug in the memory model.
defenses: Send generic messages to the client; log full details only on the server side.
Give the client a reference ID (timestamp, request ID) they can quote to support, instead of raw internals.
Define and review a logging/response policy: never echo paths, stack traces, or raw system error text externally.
Treat log output and error responses as separate channels with separate audiences.
